title: About
content: About Vinod Ashok Thale Postdoctoral Researcher, Zhejiang University Ph.D. in Engineering Mechanics, Xi'an Jiaotong University M.Tech. in Computational Fluid Dynamics, UPES Research background I work on computational fluid dynamics, with an emphasis on multiphase flows, interfacial dynamics and fluid–structure interaction. My doctoral work at Xi’an Jiaotong University focused on the numerical modelling of air-in-liquid compound drops, including impact forces and jet formation. At Zhejiang University, my research applies CFD methods to agricultural engineering and aquaculture, including drop impact and fish hydrodynamics. My work uses Basilisk for adaptive multiphase simulations and IBAMR for immersed-boundary applications. Explore research · View software

title: CV
content: Curriculum vitae Current appointment Postdoctoral Researcher , Zhejiang University, China College of Biosystems Engineering and Food Science Education Ph.D. in Engineering Mechanics , Xi’an Jiaotong University, China. M.Tech. in Computational Fluid Dynamics , University of Petroleum and Energy Studies, India. Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering , North Maharashtra University, India. Research interests Multiphase and interfacial flows; drop impact; fluid–structure interaction; immersed-boundary methods; and adaptive computational fluid dynamics. Awards and Fellowships 2018 — Chinese Government Scholarship, Xi’an Jiaotong University, China. 2017 — Junior Research Fellowship, Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO), Government of India. 2016 — Junior Research Fellowship, Indian Institute of Technology Bombay. 2016 — Junior Research Fellowship, Indian Institute of Technology Dhanbad. 2016 — Junior Research Fellowship, Defence Institute of Advanced Technology, Pune. Open-Source Software Solver modules and applications for open-source CFD frameworks, available at github.com/vinodthale . Basilisk (Basilisk C): drop-impact, aerobreakup, phase-change, and thermocapillary modules, with axisymmetric and 3D post-processing tools. IBAMR (C++, SAMRAI, ConstraintIB): fish-swimming, scalar-transport, and particle-tracking applications, with Lagrangian mesh-generation and force diagnostics. Technical Expertise HPC and software: Linux, MPI, SLURM, CMake; C/C++, CUDA, Fortran, Python, MATLAB, R, GNU Octave, LaTeX; restart and batch workflows. Other CFD tools: Gerris, OpenFOAM, ANSYS Fluent/UDFs, COMSOL Multiphysics, STAR-CCM+. Modelling and data: Physics-informed neural networks; surrogate and reduced-order models; Gnuplot, Tecplot; high-speed imaging and image processing. Engineering tools: AutoCAD, SolidWorks, FEA, LabVIEW; electrical and conductivity measurements; optical probes. Languages: English, Mandarin Chinese, Marathi, and Hindi. My work spans drop and bubble dynamics , impact forces, and fluid–structure interaction , with applications in agricultural engineering and aquaculture. title: Research
content: Research My research combines numerical methods, theory and scientific computing to study interfacial flows and fluid–structure interactions. Compound drops and interfacial flows Air-in-liquid compound drops, their impact dynamics, interface evolution, jetting and force response. Basilisk simulations are used to investigate these processes. Read the impact-force paper → Drop impact and force Drop impact on solid and liquid targets, with attention to impact force, pressure and the evolution of the liquid interface. Explore the code → IBAMR IMMERSED BOUNDARIES · ADAPTIVE MESH Fish hydrodynamics Immersed-boundary simulations of fish swimming and surrounding flows, using adaptive grids and the IBAMR framework. Explore the repository → CFD FLOW · TRANSPORT · AQUACULTURE Aquaculture and agricultural flows Applications of CFD to recirculating aquaculture systems and agricultural engineering, including flow and transport problems.
